headlines.title: How a dual language program is helping a struggling San Jose school district
headlines.description: A San Jose school district is considering reopening a campus it previously closed thanks to a successful dual language immersion program. Declining enrollment has school districts across California, including San Jose’s Alum Rock Union Elementary School District (ARUSD), facing the prospect of closing schools. ARUSD’s Ben Painter Elementary School was on the list of schools slated to potentially close due to low enrollment, but demand for its Vietnamese dual language immersion program ballooned this fall. “This year we have every classroom full,” Painter Elementary Principal Dr. Joseph Manluco said. “We have kids in every classroom with a large and growing Vietnamese dual language immersion program.” There are 420 students at Painter Elementary, a number that might bode well for other campuses that are currently shut down. “We do have other campuses within the district that are exceeding enrollment, where they need more room,” ARUSD Superintendent Dr. Marnie Hazelton said. “We are working with committees along with our board members and a local real estate agency to see if it is a viable option to reopen some of these campuses.” Pew Research estimates San Jose has the largest population of Vietnamese people outside of Vietnam at roughly 150,000. Painter Elementary’s program is the second largest Vietnamese dual language immersion program in Northern California. The idea is to combine quality academics with a second language. But there are plenty of non-Vietnamese American students on campus. “We have students in here that are becoming trilingual or even quadrilingual,” Manluco said.

headlines.title: Highway 37 in North Bay to close this weekend for El Niño storm preps
headlines.description: Highway 37 in the North Bay will shut down in both directions this weekend to allow Caltrans crews time to raise the flood-prone area ahead of a potentially powerful El Niño and winter storms. Motorists traveling through the area should expect significant delays and increased travel times. Here’s what to know about the closure and detour information. When will Highway 37 shut down? The closure on the highway starts at 10 p.m. Friday. Caltrans expects to reopen lanes by 5 a.m. Monday. What part of Highway 37 will close during weekend closure? Highway 37 will shut down between Mare Island in Vallejo and Sears Point in Sonoma County, according to Caltrans. Detour information for Highway 37 closure Motorists traveling on eastbound Highway 37 during the closure will exit left onto northbound Highway 121 in Sonoma; Make a right on Highway 12, 1(Carneros Hwy) and continue; Right on Highway 12/Highway 29; Enter left for the connector loop off-ramp back to eastbound Highway 37. Motorists traveling on westbound Highway 37 will exit right onto northbound Highway 29 in Napa, and follow Highway 29 to westbound Highway 12, then to southbound Highway 121; Why is Caltrans shutting down Highway 37? Highway 37 near Mare Island has flooded repeatedly over the years. Caltrans said the work is designed to help reduce flooding risks on the vital commuter route. headlines.title: Pacifica Pier repairs cause traffic headaches
headlines.description: Major repairs at the Pacifica Pier are causing traffic headaches for people in the area. Construction crews are expected to begin moving a large crane to the shore Thursday, which will be used to stabilize the cracked pier. It could take crews up to five days to position the crane, while the overall repair phase is expected to last at least three months. The pier has been closed since June, when engineers discovered major cracking.

headlines.title: Preliminary 3.0 magnitude earthquake strikes near Hollister
headlines.description: A preliminary 3.0 magnitude earthquake struck near Hollister, according to the United States Geological Survey. The quake hit at 2:58 p.m. and was centered 14.6 miles south-southeast of Hollister, the USGS said. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates. headlines.title: Oakland's 911 system goes down, calls routed to Alameda County
headlines.description: All 911 calls in Oakland are being transferred to the Alameda County Sheriff’s Office. Oakland Police Department (OPD) dispatchers noticed that their computer systems started freezing around 9 p.m. Wednesday. Dispatchers tried both emergency and non-emergency lines and discovered there was no service to phone lines and internet. OPD dispatchers were moved to the Oakland Fire and Alameda County Sheriff’s dispatch center. Oakland police said they are only responding to priority one calls as the IT department looks to restore services with AT&T.

headlines.title: Ethics tip takes center stage in Sheng Thao corruption trial
headlines.description: An ethics tip is at the center of testimony Thursday as the federal corruption trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao continues in Oakland. Thao, her longtime partner Andre Jones and businessmen David and Andy Duong are accused of conspiracy, bribery and wire fraud. An FBI agent was back on the stand Thursday, with some of the evidence presented directly connecting Thao and her three co-defendants to political mailers that sparked the federal investigation. Sheng Thao Oct 15 Sheng Thao Oct 19 Sheng Thao Oct 13 Thao arrived at the federal courthouse in Oakland after a two-day court recess. Jones and the Duongs were also in court Thursday morning. The FBI agent continued to detail how Thao, Jones and the Duongs came to be under federal investigation. The FBI raided Thao’s Oakland home in June 2024, along with three properties tied to the Duong family. The FBI agent testified that evidence from phones, iPads, USB drives, hard drives, computers, phone records and disappearing messages showed that Thao allegedly knew about political mailers that led to an ethics tip to the FBI. The agent previously testified that the deal for the mailers indicated a larger bribery scheme and a list of favors allegedly owed to the Duongs in exchange for their help getting Thao elected. Thao, Jones and the Duongs face charges of conspiracy, bribery and wire fraud. All four have pleaded not guilty.

headlines.title: Westbound I-80 in San Francisco near the Bay Bridge to close this weekend
headlines.description: A section of westbound Interstate 80 in San Francisco near the Bay Bridge will be closed this weekend for a construction project. The full westbound I-80 closure from Fifth Street to 15th Street is scheduled to start at 11 p.m. Friday and continue until 6 a.m. Monday, according to Caltrans. Motorists should avoid using the Bay Bridge to get into San Francisco during the closure, Caltrans said. Alternate options include taking public transportation or using the San Mateo, Dumbarton or Richmond-San Rafael bridges. “This work is necessary for crews to place polyester concrete on the WB I-80 Bayshore freeway deck and will complete a broader I-80 Bayshore Freeway viaduct polyester concrete placement project which began on the eastbound I-80 Bayshore Freeway earlier this year,” Caltrans said in a statement. The map below provides a closer look at the closure details and detour options.

headlines.title: 71-year-old man dies after being struck by self-driving car on I-80 in Vallejo
headlines.description: A 71-year-old man was killed early Thursday morning after he was struck by a self-driving car as he was crossing Interstate 80 in Vallejo, the California Highway Patrol said. According to the CHP’s Solano-area office, officers were alerted to a collision reported around 2:35 a.m. on westbound I-80 at the I-780 interchange. When they arrived, first responders found the severely injured pedestrian, who was later declared dead. The driver of the involved vehicle, a 26-year-old San Francisco man, stayed at the scene and told CHP officers that his vehicle, a Tesla, was being operated in Full Self-Driving autonomous mode when it hit the pedestrian. According to the CHP, the Tesla had full footage of the crash since it was recorded by the vehicle’s dashcam. Based on the video, the Tesla was traveling around 70 mph when the pedestrian entered the freeway. He began crossing toward the center divider from the right shoulder, placing him directly in front of the Tesla. “The video showed the Tesla’s brakes being applied as the vehicle steered to the left in an effort to avoid the pedestrian. Despite these evasive actions, the right front portion of the Tesla struck the individual,” the CHP said in a statement on social media. The agency said the 71-year-old was again struck by at least one more vehicle while lying in the traffic lanes, adding that no other vehicles stopped to cooperate with authorities. The other involved vehicle or driver is yet to be identified. “The Solano Area CHP extends its deepest condolences to the family and friends of the deceased during this difficult time,” the agency said. Anyone who may have witnessed the crash or who has information regarding the other vehicles involved is encouraged to contact the CHP Solano-area office at 707-639-5600.

headlines.title: Video game developer BioWare shuts down, next ‘Mass Effect' canceled amid broader layoffs at EA
headlines.description: Video game publisher Electronic Arts is shutting down the popular and influential game development studio BioWare after more than three decades. The upcoming “Mass Effect” game, the fifth since 2007, has been canceled. BioWare announced the closure on social media Wednesday following a report by Bloomberg that also said the company is laying off 400 people, including about 50 at BioWare. The Redwood Shores, California-based maker of popular titles like “Battlefield” and “The Sims” closed the $55 billion sale of its business to Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund PIF, investment firm Silver Lake Partners and Affinity Partners, which is run by President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, in August. Representatives for EA did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment on the layoffs. “What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember,” the studio said via social media. “These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with characters, and made these worlds your own.” BioWare built its reputation on immersive role-playing adventures, from sword-and-sorcery fantasies like “Baldur’s Gate” and “Dragon Age” to science fiction epics like “Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic” and “Mass Effect.” But its effort to branch out into multiplayer shooters, 2019’s “Anthem,” steered away from the studio’s strength as a creator of compelling single-player narratives. It failed to find the sort of loyal audience that keeps online hits like “Fortnite” and “Overwatch” humming. Meanwhile the latest installments of its two most popular original franchises — 2017’s “Mass Effect: Andromeda” and 2024’s “Dragon Age: The Veilguard” — met with mixed reviews and disappointed many fans. A new chapter of “Mass Effect” was in development before BioWare announced its shutdown. BioWare, based in Canada, was founded in 1995 and acquired by EA in 2007. __ Associated Press Writer Lou Kesten in Washington contributed.

headlines.title: Federal judge orders Trump administration to halt noncitizen voting investigation in 9 states
headlines.description: A federal judge in California has ordered the Trump administration to halt investigations in nine states into whether noncitizens are registered to vote. U.S. District Court Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin in Oakland found the government’s effort is relying on data that is full of errors and that it’s leading to intimidation of groups performing voter assistance efforts. She said it should be halted until polls close on Election Day, Nov. 3. She put her ruling, which was made Wednesday, on hold until Friday to give the administration a chance to appeal. The ruling applies to investigations in California, Connecticut, Georgia, Missouri, Nevada, New York, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wisconsin. It comes as the Trump administration has been hunting for noncitizen voters throughout the country in the months leading into the midterm elections. The administration has signaled that it’s a major problem, when in fact it’s quite rare, as even its own investigations have shown. The lawsuit was filed by the California Nurses Association and National Nurses United, along with the Voto Latino Foundation, San Francisco and Santa Clara County. In response to the ruling, the Department of Homeland Security issued an email statement Thursday saying it’s focused on “removing aliens who vote and dilute the votes of U.S. citizens,” while adding, “We have no plans to question or investigate people we believe to be U.S. citizens.” According to legal filings in the case, investigators were told to target naturalized citizens to see whether they had voted before they became U.S. citizens. The lists of voters to check came from sources that included state and local governments and publicly available information. Martinez-Olguin called them “voluminous and unreliable.” “Even under the best conditions, there is a high likelihood of error in review because there is no federal database containing citizenship status of U.S. residents,” Martinez-Olguin wrote in her ruling. “The time limitations implemented during the Surge further exacerbate the risk of error.” The Department of Justice has been demanding detailed and unredacted voter roll data from the states and has sued the 30 states that have refused to turn it over, losing each of those cases so far. The judge noted that for states that refused to share their records, the administration was trying to obtain them through “unreliable commercial versions of voter roll data.” She said during a “surge” phase of the investigation starting in late August, agents were ordered to complete reviews of flagged individuals taking no more than 12 minutes per person to assess whether they were legally qualified to vote. In their challenge, the plaintiffs said some U.S. citizens felt they were wrongly identified and investigated as part of the probe. Martinez-Olguin said those fears “are well understood as intimidation” that has chilled people from attending campaign events and working as poll monitors during the election. Beau Tremitiere, a lawyer representing the unions and voter group, said in a statement that the ruling affirms the groups’ position. “It was clear from the start that DHS built its lists on bad data, never checked how often it was wrong, and recklessly sent agents to people’s homes weeks before an election,” Tremitiere said. Details of the investigation, known as the “Unlawful Voter Initiative,” came to light last month after Democratic Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York and Democratic Sen. Alex Padilla of California released a whistleblower report about it.

headlines.title: San Jose community pushes to rebuild MACSA youth center destroyed by fire
headlines.description: A San Jose neighborhood is working to rebuild a center that it says was the heart of the community. The building that once housed the MACSA youth center in the Mayfair community burned to the ground in August of last year. At the time, community members told NBC Bay Area what the center meant to them and their families. Since then, neighbors and activists have been pushing for it to be rebuilt to serve the community. In May, the rebuild was approved by the Alum Rock School District. Somos Mayfair was a major proponent of retaining the cultural aspect of the building that had been shuttered. San Jose City Councilmember Peter Ortiz also lent his voice to the cause. “MACSA center was a safe place for our youth, especially the ones impacted in gangs,” Ortiz said. A MACSA input session will be held Thursday at the Mayfair Community Center from 4:30 to 7 p.m. The session is directed at students and their families, as the goal is to create a youth center that will serve them.

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website.
